components.note: 十 (ten, suggesting abundance) — relates to 华's meaning 'flowery, splendid,' an abundance of blossoms.
化 (huà) gives a sound hint — 华 is pronounced huá, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
皿 (dish) — 盛 relates to filling a dish or vessel to abundance.
成 (chéng) gives a sound distantly related to shèng, having drifted apart over time.
页 (head) — 顿 originally related to bowing the head, i.e. a pause or stop
屯 (tún) gives a sound distantly related to 顿's reading dùn, having drifted apart over time
女 (woman) — 姐 names a female relative, an older sister.
且 (qiě) gives the rhyme, close to jiě though the tone differs.
女 (woman) — 妹 names a female relative, a younger sister.
未 (wèi) gives a rhyme close to mèi, with a different initial.
礻 (an altar, related to ritual/spirits) — 神 relates to gods and spirits.
申 (shēn) gives a hint of the sound — 神 is pronounced shén, a connection that has shifted over time.
禾 (grain) — an older sense of 秘 was linked to grain kept out of sight, before it narrowed to 'secret.'
必 (bì) gives the sound — an exact match with 秘.
王 (a variant of 玉, meaning jade) — a valuable object one might glimpse or notice.
见 (to see) — catching sight of something links to the meanings 'to appear, present, now.'

正 (zhèng) gives the sound — 政 is also pronounced zhèng, an exact match.
氵 (water) — 治 relates to managing or controlling the flow of water, such as flood control.
台 (a platform, structure) — a structure used to direct and control water gave 治 its meaning 'to govern' or 'to manage.'
⺮ (bamboo) — ancient texts were written on bound bamboo strips, and 第 originally referred to the sequential order of such strips, giving rise to its meaning 'ordinal number' (as in 第一, first).
囗 (an enclosure) — 四 pictures a bounded space.
儿 (a person) — a person enclosed within four walls gave 四 its meaning 'four,' though the exact link to the number is debated.
鬼 (ghost) — 魔 names a demon or evil spirit.
麻 (má) gives a sound distantly related to mó, having drifted apart over time.

子 (child) — 孤 originally described a child without a parent, an orphan.
瓜 (guā) gives a sound close to gū, sharing the same initial.
犭 (dog) — an old link behind 独's meaning 'alone, single, solitary'
虫 (chóng) gives a loose sound connection to 独's reading dú
冂 (an enclosure or doorway) — 内 pictures the space one enters.
人 (person) — a person entering an enclosure gave 内 its meaning 'inside' or 'within.'
宀 (roof/house) — 容's meaning 'to contain, hold' relates to a house holding things, extended to 'appearance, to allow, tolerate.'
巨 depicts a hand gripping a large carpenter's square, a tool for measuring right angles — an image linked to great size, giving 巨 its meaning 'huge, giant.'

Heart/mind — punishment is meant to affect one's conscience.
Gives the sound zhēng, related to chéng but drifted apart over time.
罒 (a net) — historically linked to wrongdoing and being caught out.
刂 (a knife/blade) — carrying out punishment, together giving 罚 its meaning 'to punish, penalize.'
力 (strength) — 加 pictures adding one's effort to a cause.
口 (mouth, words) — combining strength with words of support gave 加 its meaning 'to add' or 'to increase.'
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.

meanings: (lit. and fig.) to open a door

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — depicts hands at work.
一 represents the latch or bar of a door; hands lifting it away gave 开 its meaning 'to open, to start.'
门 is a picture of a double-leafed door or gate, drawn symmetrically to show two swinging panels.
艹 (grass/plant) — 蓝 originally named the indigo plant used to make blue dye.
监 (jiān) gives a sound distantly related to lán, having drifted apart over time.
⺈ (a person, bent over) — the figure whose outward expression is being depicted.
巴 — traditionally linked to desire or emotion, so together the character points to a person's expression or complexion, extended to 色's meaning 'color, appearance.'
辶 (to walk) — 退 relates to moving backward or away
艮 (gèn) gives a sound distantly related to 退's reading tuì, having drifted apart over time
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
The 田-shaped top pictures a large, strange head.
儿-shaped legs below trace a crouching, spindly body, together giving 鬼 the shape of a ghostly figure.
鬼 (ghost/spirit) — 魂 names a person's spirit or soul.
云 (yún) gives a rhyme close to hún, with a different initial.
又 (hand) and 寸 (also derived from a hand shape) — together suggesting two hands matching or corresponding, related to 对's meaning 'correct, matching.'
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.
辶 (to walk) — 进 relates to advancing or entering, both movement-related.
井 (jǐng) gives a close sound cue — 进 is pronounced jìn, sharing similar consonant and vowel sounds.
夭 depicts a person leaning to one side, arms swinging — here the pose of walking high up on stilts, giving 乔 its meaning 'tall, lofty.'
氵 (water) — 治 relates to managing or controlling the flow of water, such as flood control.
台 (a platform, structure) — a structure used to direct and control water gave 治 its meaning 'to govern' or 'to manage.'
礻 (an altar, related to ritual/spirits) — 神 relates to gods and spirits.
申 (shēn) gives a hint of the sound — 神 is pronounced shén, a connection that has shifted over time.
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a rider.
可 here is said to depict a mount — a person riding in an unusual way gave 奇 its meaning 'strange, odd, remarkable.'
牛 (ox) on the left is the animal being tended.
攵 (a hand holding a stick) on the right shows someone driving or herding it, giving 牧 its meaning 'to herd, to tend livestock.'
帀 (a banner or covering) — flying above the scene.
刂 (a knife) — wielded with skill beneath the banner, an image of expertise giving 师 its meaning 'master, teacher, expert.'
干 (originally a person) shown carrying a heavy load of grain on their back — since harvests came once a year, the character came to mean 'year.'
纟 (thread) — 级 originally named a strand or rank of silk thread, extended to 'grade, level, rank.'
及 (jí) gives the sound — 级 is also pronounced jí, an exact match.
王 (a variant of 玉, jade) — 环 originally referred to a round jade ring or bracelet
不 (bù) gives a sound distantly related to 环's reading huán, having drifted apart considerably over time
土 (earth) — 境 relates to land and territory, extended to mean 'environment, boundary'
竟 (jìng) gives the sound — 境 is also pronounced jìng, an exact match
扌 (hand) — 提 relates to lifting or carrying something by hand.
是 (shì) gives a hint of the sound — 提 is pronounced tí, a connection that has shifted over time.
至 (zhì, to arrive) — carries 到's core meaning, 'to reach, to arrive'
刂 (a form of 刀, dāo) gives a sound close to 到's pronunciation dào
禾 (grain/rice plant) — 种 relates to seeds and planting crops.
中 (zhōng) gives the sound — 种 is pronounced zhǒng, matching aside from tone.
刂 (knife) — 刺 describes the action of piercing or stabbing with something sharp.
朿 (cì) gives the sound — an exact match with 刺's reading cì.
氵 (water) — 激 originally described water dashing or surging forcefully
敫 (jiǎo) gives a sound distantly related to 激's reading jī, having drifted apart over time
Originally depicted a hand 扌 gripping a weapon 戈; this original meaning was later borrowed to represent the pronoun 'I/we.'
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'
见 (to see) — 规 originally named a craftsman's compass, a tool used to observe and measure circles, extended to 'rule, regulation.'
夫 (fū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from guī.
宀 (roof) — represents a home or fixed dwelling.
疋 (a foot/person) — a person settling down under a roof gave 定 its meaning 'to decide, to fix, to settle.'
女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'
夕 (evening/night), doubled — two nights stacked together suggested the idea of accumulation, giving 多 its meaning of 'many, much.'
言 (speech) — 警 relates to speaking out a warning or alarm
敬 (jìng) gives a sound close to 警's reading jǐng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
长 (simplified from 長) depicts an elderly figure with long flowing hair and a cane — length and seniority are linked in the original picture.
日 (sun) — 最 pictures something happening under the sun, that is, everywhere.
取 (to take, gather) — combined with the sun above, gathering everything under the sun gave 最 its meaning of 'most' or 'the utmost.'
亻 (person) shows 佳 describes a positive quality, often applied to people or things.
圭 (guī) gives a sound distantly related to jiā, having drifted apart over time.
爫 (a hand, from above) — 受 pictures something being passed.
又 (a hand, from below) — one hand giving and another receiving gave 受 its meaning 'to receive' or 'to endure.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
发 (fā) gives a sound related to fèi, sharing the initial f-, though the rhyme has drifted from ā to èi over time.
讠 (speech) — 话 relates to speaking and words.
舌 (tongue) — the organ used for speaking, reinforcing 话's meaning of 'speech' or 'words.'
攵 (an action/to strike) — 效 relates to the result produced by an action
交 (jiāo) gives a sound close to 效's reading xiào
田 (here representing round fruit, not its usual meaning 'field') — 果 pictures fruit hanging from branches.
木 (tree) — fruit growing on a tree gave 果 its meaning 'fruit' and, more broadly, 'result.'
口 is a simple picture of an open mouth.
鬼 (ghost) — 魔 names a demon or evil spirit.
麻 (má) gives a sound distantly related to mó, having drifted apart over time.
氵 (water/stream) — water naturally follows a fixed course, an image linked to the idea of 'law' or 'method.'
去 (to go/a course) — the path a stream follows suggested a regulated, consistent way of doing things, hence 'law, method.'
犭 (dog) — an old link behind 独's meaning 'alone, single, solitary'
虫 (chóng) gives a loose sound connection to 独's reading dú
A picture of a nose; because people in ancient China would point to their own nose when referring to themselves, the character came to mean 'self.'
王 (a variant of 玉, meaning jade) — a valuable object one might glimpse or notice.
见 (to see) — catching sight of something links to the meanings 'to appear, present, now.'
金 depicts a bell or metal casting mold, with dots representing droplets of molten metal — a picture linked to metal and, later, specifically gold.

meanings: to understand sth well and know how to use it

components.note: 手 (hand) — 掌 names the palm, part of the hand.
尚 (shàng) gives a rhyme close to zhǎng, with the initial shifted.
扌 (hand) — 握 describes an action done with the hand: grasping tightly.
屋 (wū) gives a sound distantly related to wò, having drifted apart over time.
龶-shaped top pictures a ripe stalk of grain.
夂 below pictures roots or a foot, together giving 麦 its meaning 'wheat.'
十 (here representing a weapon or armor) — 克 pictures overcoming an opponent.
兄 (a person, here representing a formidable figure) — overcoming a strong opponent gave 克 its meaning 'to overcome' or 'to be able to.'
儿 (simplified from 兒) depicts a small child, drawn with a large head on a small body — a simple picture of youth.
立 (standing) — a small figure standing upright.
里 here representing a village or settlement, together giving 童 its meaning 'child.'
女 depicts a kneeling figure with arms crossed, a traditional posture — a simple picture of a woman.
子 (child) — 孩 relates directly to children
亥 (hài) gives a sound close to 孩's reading hái
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.
弓 (bow) — a strong bow that took great force to draw gave 强 its meaning 'strong, powerful.'
虫 was a different phonetic element historically; its pronunciation has shifted so far from qiáng over time that the sound link is no longer obvious.
A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
八 (to divide/split apart) — represents something already split into parts.
刀 (knife) — a knife cutting already-divided pieces further, giving 分 its meaning 'to divide, to separate.'
廾 (two hands) — depicts hands at work.
一 represents the latch or bar of a door; hands lifting it away gave 开 its meaning 'to open, to start.'
承 depicts multiple hands supporting and lifting something from below — giving 承 its meaning 'to support, to receive, to inherit.'
讠 (speech) — 诺 relates to a spoken promise or agreement.
若 (ruò) gives a rhyme close to nuò, sharing a related initial.
⺼ (flesh) — 脖 names a body part, the neck.
孛 (bèi) gives a sound close to bó, sharing the same initial.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.
木 (wood) — 检 originally related to a wooden tally or label used for checking records
佥 (qiān) gives a sound distantly related to 检's reading jiǎn, having drifted apart over time
宀 (roof) — 察 relates to careful observation
祭 (jì) gives a loose sound connection to 察's reading chá

meanings: (of a movie, book, TV show etc) good

components.note: 女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'
手 (hand) — depicts a hand raised above the eyes.
目 (eye) — shielding the eyes with a hand to look into the distance gave 看 its meaning 'to look, to see.'
